item.title: Decode drill: MOV r/m8, imm8
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
Decode this instruction:
C6 41 03 41
What is the assembly? Which operand is the immediate, and how many bytes does it write?
ANSWER mov byte ptr [rcx+3], 0x41
- C6 /0 ib is MOV r/m8, imm8. ModRM 41 = 01 000 001: mod=01 (disp8 follows), reg=000 (the /0 opcode extension, not a register), rm=001 (rcx base). Then 03 = disp8, 41 = imm8. - The immediate always comes last, after the displacement. It writes exactly one byte ('A') to rcx+3; neighbouring bytes are untouched. - In C: ((char*)p)[3] = 'A'; with p in rcx (Windows x64 first argument).
